pr_body:
Fixes paritally https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/95921.

We used to throw PNSE for all `HashCode` functions. The consequence was throwing PNSE for quite a few APIs, some of them crucial and far-connected with Globalization. With this PR the following APIs do not throw PNSE always (see the update in the doc for details):
```
- System.Collections.Hashtable.Add 
- System.Collections.Hashtable.GetHash 
- System.Collections.CaseInsensitiveHashCodeProvider.GetHashCode 
- System.Collections.Specialized.NameValueCollection.Add 
- System.Collections.Specialized.NameValueCollection.Remove 
- System.Collections.Specialized.NameValueCollection.Get 
- System.Collections.Specialized.NameValueCollection.Set 
- System.Collections.Specialized.NameObjectCollectionBase.BaseAdd 
- System.Collections.Specialized.NameObjectCollectionBase.BaseGet 
- System.Collections.Specialized.NameObjectCollectionBase.BaseRemove 
- System.Collections.Specialized.NameObjectCollectionBase.BaseSet 
- System.Collections.Specialized.OrderedDictionary.Add 
- System.Collections.Generic.HashSet 
- System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary
```
 JS does not expose native, locale-sensitive hashing that we could use, so we decided to utilize Invariant version of functions instead with some limitations. Invariant hashing algorithm differs from ICU hashing with not ignoring empty unicode chars (e.g. zero width joiner), the strings get cleaned from them first. 
- Invariant locale - always supported with this PR by using invariant hashing method. This approach differs from the ICU approach where invariant culture was getting data from ICU4C.
- Non-invariant locales with `CompareOptions.None` - use invariant hashing algo.
- Non-invariant locales with `CompareOptions.IgnoreCase` - use JS-native toLower() and then invariant hashing algo.
- Non-invariant locales with any other CompareOptions e.g. `CompareOptions.IgnoreCase | CompareOptions.IgnoreSymbols` - keep throwing PNSE, as it was without this PR.

It will be documented in the HG doc, so far I did not find an example where the behavior of APIs that threw PNSE so far differs between ICU and HG because of this change.

## Out of scope (for follow-up PRs):
- performance tests for methods using `HashCode` and performance improvements
- `SortKey` - investigate similar change

issue_context.title: [browser] Limit PNSE in `HybridGlobalization`
issue_context.body:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/95920 updated the doc with APIs that are throwing PlatformNotSupportedException by design. Consider:
- implementing invariant `SortKey` in HybridGlobalization
- changing comparison options to supported ones.

`SortKey`:
- JS does not expose API that would give us similar information to `SortKey`
- `Intl.Collator`-based implementation of `SortKey` could be an alternative to the original, locale-sensitive `SortKey`. However, we have no guarantee that the implementation would give similar results and would not cost us too much space.
- Invariant SortKey does not cover fully the original, locale-sensitive functionality, however it is the best alternative when it comes to saving space - it's already implemented, we would reuse existing code. Document the changes in behavior.

`CompareOptions`:
- some combinations of compare options are not supported (see the doc)
- APIs in other, non-globalization libs use these combinations, becoming not supported
- Check if they would not work equally good with another compare options set that is supported and document the changes in behavior.

Old issue discussing the possibilities:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/84621

review_comments:
`CompareInfo.WebAssembly.cs` file is added under this condition:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/77d643d8678d0cae1144557f106bb693a1cbca25/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System.Private.CoreLib.Shared.projitems#L344
could you please elaborate ? Should this throw PNSE if it behaves wrongly ?

It used to throw PNSE, but this behavior prevented a lot of APIs to be used, even far connected with Globalization, e.g. `System.Collections.Hashtable.Add()`. We decided to allow the APIs to work but with a restriction that they would share the HashCode and SortKey functions with Invariant mode. Because this test is not expected to work with Invariant mode (`PlatformDetection.IsIcuGlobalization` means that it should work only in ICU, not with Invariant), then it's a natural consequence that now for Hybrid it won't be expected to work either - it uses Invariant logic underneath.

Should I maybe change the comment to be more descriptive? Like, "HybridGlobalization on Browser uses Invariant HashCode and SortKey, so its effect does not match this of ICU. This test is not run in InvariantGlobalization - IsIcuGlobalization=false then."
I'm OK with the test change now. I'm also ok about `HashCode` because I understand that those could have collisions.

I don't understand if different algo for SortKey would lead to different ordering in the results of the actual data. If so, that could be "wrong" and unexpected. I'm not sure what needs to be done about it.
If we are now **consistently** sorting invariant style in all places, that would be acceptable hybrid trade off. We just need to document it properly.

Do you suggest adding info to docs/design/features/globalization-hybrid-mode.md? Or is it sufficient? There is a list of known APIs that might be affected + info that Invariant SortKey is used for them.
Hmm, about `HashCode`, it would be OK to have more collisions, but this is making less collisions. Things which do string equal don't do hash equals. That breaks the the contract, I think.
This is just moving the code to separate method. But I'm not sure about the method name. It seems like more than pure invariant. There is also ignore-case considered.

The method is called when `if (!GlobalizationMode.Invariant)`, so it is invariant way of hashing, based on the `CompareOptions` passed to the method. I do not see anything misleading in the name." There is also ignore-case considered." - it can be deduced looking at the arguments passed to the method
could you please explain the consequences ?
I will update the description, one of the consequences is quite severe: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/96400.
